text:
alice: Putting this here — Sales asked for firm p95=150ms, p99=450ms for Nimbus pilot. Current prod runs p95 ~160ms, p99 ~620ms at their QPS. Profiling attached. Need runtime/eng input on whether we can hit p99 without dropping throughput or doing carveouts.

raj: saw the profiling. Main tail is KV cold misses + kernel A's slow attention kernel at long seq. If we pick kernel B we drop token throughput ~18% but p99 drops to ~310ms in sim.

maria: microbatching tuning might help: for this workload avg seq=256, microbatch=1 keeps latency but wastes GPU. microbatch=3 gives much better throughput but p99 jumps. We can try dynamic microbatching with per-request deadline.

sam_sales: customer will pay for dedicated but wants '99s' guarantee. They said p95 is ok at 150 but p99 is a hard requirement at 450. Any blunt tradeoffs will affect price.

raj: quick numbers from local run (QPS 20, single GPU): kernel A, mb=1 => p95 154ms, p99 620ms, tkn/s 12k. kernel B, mb=1 => p95 168ms, p99 310ms, tkn/s 9.8k.

alice: so kernel B improves tail but hurts throughput. Are there KV cache warmup options? Nimbus has a lot of unique prefixes.

maria: KV cache TTL and proactive warming help. If we prewarm top-10k keys + prefix caching, p99 drops ~120ms across configs but costs warmup CPU + memory. For this customer estimate extra mem ~16GB per shard.

raj: also saw perf regression in latest kernel commit c3f9 — that increased attention kernel latency at seq>512. Not in release yet but blocking if we pick kernel A path. Opening PR to revert.

canary-bot: Canary run #452 failed p99 threshold on kernel A, attached logs: `latency spikes at 00:04:12`.

maria: Proposal: For Nimbus pilot, do kernel B + KV prewarm + dynamic microbatching: start mb=1 for first 30s of a session then ramp to mb=2-3. Expected outcome: p95 ~170ms, p99 ~320-360ms, throughput -12%. Evaluate with canary.

sam_sales: Customer asks if we can add fallback: if p99 starts breaching, route 10% of requests to larger-capacity nodes or drop to simpler model. Is that feasible?

raj: yes, routing policy doable. We can implement target-aware routing and fallback to a higher-capacity pool (or smaller model) automatically. Need config + SLA language.

alice: action items: (1) raj revert kernel regression PR and bench both kernels (2) maria run prewarm config with mem/cost estimate (3) eng-ops add routing/fallback config and canary (4) sam formalize customer carveouts and pricing. Ping me when canary ready. :thumbsup:

sam_sales: I'll prep the customer note with options + cost delta.

raj: started the revert PR 2381, running bench now. Will post numbers in this thread.

maria: baseline warmup script attached inside gist: ```bash
# prewarm top prefixes
python scripts/prewarm_kv.py --keys 10000 --shards 8
``` will run in ~6m per shard.

alice: thanks all. keep updates short in thread. We'll aim for canary by EOD Thu.
